Run a test that checks the Share button visibility at 375px and 768px.

K-003524.check: grep prints 1 or more, Playwright reports the Share button as hidden at 375px and visible at 768px, and axe reports no violations.

steps.do: Build the Tailwind stylesheet from the input file into the dist folder.
Count how many rules in the built CSS use margin-inline-start.
Count how many rules in the built CSS use margin-inline-end.
Confirm no physical margin-left rule was generated by the logical classes.

K-003525.check: margin-inline-start and margin-inline-end each return a count of 1 or more, and margin-left returns 0.
traps: Small models assume the build failed when rg prints nothing; a zero count is a valid result, so read the number.
Do not edit dist/app.css by hand, because the next build overwrites it. Change the source classes in src instead.
Check the Tailwind version in package.json first, because logical classes like ms- need Tailwind 3.3 or newer.

steps.do: Change into the project root.
Install the project dependencies for the test runner.
Run the layout test that loads each locale and checks the scroll width of every nav button against its client width.
Use a German string of about 40 characters in the button label fixture and check that the label truncates or wraps inside a width of 160px.

K-003526.example: The German fixture for the Save button is Speichern und fortfahren, which is 28 characters, and the button is 160px wide. The Playwright test loads the page with lang=de and expects scrollWidth less than or equal to clientWidth for every button.
K-003526.check: npx playwright test prints 0 failed tests, and the overflow assertion reports scrollWidth less than or equal to clientWidth for every button.
traps: Small models use a short English test string and miss real overflow; use the longest translation in the locale files.
Fixed width containers hide overflow with overflow-hidden, which makes the test pass while the text is cut off, so check the visible text too.
Do not accept a passing test if the locale file is missing; confirm the German and Arabic JSON files exist first.

steps.do: Start the dev server in the background so the locale page responds on port 3000.
Run axe against the Arabic route and exit with a non-zero code if any violation is found.
Run axe against the Hebrew route in the same way.
Check the lang and dir attributes on the rendered html element for the Arabic route.

K-003527.check: Each npx axe command reports 0 violations, and the curl output contains lang=ar and dir=rtl in the opening html tag.

A page with lang=en and dir=rtl set by hand is still wrong; the lang must match the locale.
Axe checks the DOM after load only, so run it on the page after client-side language switching finishes.

steps.do: Run Lighthouse against the Arabic route and keep only the accessibility category to shorten the run.
Read the accessibility score from the Lighthouse report and confirm it is 0.90 or higher.
Confirm each tap target in the RTL nav is at least 44px tall, using the target-size audit in the Lighthouse output.
Rerun the same Lighthouse command after a fix to confirm the score did not drop.

K-003528.example: The Arabic nav scores 0.94 on accessibility, and the target-size audit reports one link at 36px height. Increase that link to min-h-11 in Tailwind, which is 44px, and the audit passes on the next run.
K-003528.check: The Lighthouse accessibility score is 0.90 or higher, and the target-size audit lists no tap target under 44px.
traps: Small models read the score as a percentage with the decimal point in the wrong place; 0.90 means 90 out of 100.
Do not change a font size to hit a tap target; use min-h-11 or py-3 to reach 44px without altering the text.
Lighthouse runs against the built or dev server, so an unbuilt page can score differently from production.

steps.do: Change into the project root that holds the src folder.
List every physical spacing and position class in src with line numbers.

Rerun the physical-class search. It must print nothing, which means zero matching lines remain.
steps.cmd: rg -c -e ml- -e mr- -e pl- -e pr- -e left- -e right- src

K-003529.example: A card header in src/components/Header.tsx used ml-4 and right-2, so it becomes ms-4 and end-2. After the swap, rg -c prints no lines for src, and the Playwright run reports 0 failed.
K-003529.check: The second rg -c prints no lines, so zero physical classes remain in src, and npx playwright test reports 0 failed with the 16px and 8px assertions passing.

Do not use rtl:ml-0 style overrides. Use the logical ms- class instead, because it flips automatically with dir.
Text alignment classes such as text-left and text-right are not matched by this card. Change them by hand to text-start and text-end.
Check the installed Tailwind version with npm ls tailwindcss. The ms-, me-, ps-, pe-, start-, and end- names need Tailwind 3.3 or later, or v4.

steps.do: Change into the project root that holds the src folder.
List every flex-row class in src with line numbers so you can decide which rows mirror.
Record the baseline count of flex-row lines per file.

Open the pager file, check that its flex-row holds direction-bearing controls and not digits or code, then add rtl:flex-row-reverse beside flex-row. Run this once per file, because a second run doubles the class.
Count the rtl:flex-row-reverse classes in src. The count must equal the number of rows you changed.
Run the RTL row spec. It must report 0 failed. The spec asserts that under dir=rtl the Next button's bounding box x is less than the Previous button's x, and the gap is 8px (2 units).

K-003530.example: A pager in src/components/Pager.tsx has flex-row gap-2 with a Previous button and a Next button. After the change it has flex-row rtl:flex-row-reverse gap-2, so Next appears on the left in an Arabic page.
K-003530.check: rg -c rtl:flex-row-reverse prints a count per file that matches the rows you changed, and npx playwright test reports 0 failed with Next's x less than Previous's x under dir=rtl.
traps: Small models often write flex-row-reverse without the rtl: prefix, which reverses the layout in every language. Always keep the rtl: prefix.
Do not mirror rows that hold numbers, phone digits, or code, because those should stay in reading order.
Running the sed command twice on one file adds the class twice. Check the file before and after each run.
The rtl: variant in Tailwind v4 needs an ancestor with dir=rtl, so check the html or wrapper tag too.

steps.do: Create src/components/EditableTable.jsx and keep rows in useState with an errors object keyed by row id.
Call the validator inside the change handler so each edit updates the errors state for that row id.
Set aria-invalid on the input only when an error exists for that row and field.
Run the component test file to confirm the error appears after an invalid edit.
Run eslint on the component file to confirm it has no lint errors.

K-003531.example: Typing an empty name into row 3 sets errors['3'].name to 'Name is required' and that input gets aria-invalid='true'. The vitest run prints 'Tests 1 passed' for the invalid-edit case.
K-003531.check: npx vitest run prints 'Tests 1 passed' and eslint prints no output with exit code 0.
traps: Keying errors by array index breaks after a row is deleted or sorted, so use a stable id.
Mutating the rows array in place skips the re-render, so copy the array before changing a row.
Leaving aria-invalid off the input means assistive technology never learns the cell is invalid.

steps.do: Create src/lib/validators.js and export pure functions that return an error string or null.
Add a required validator that returns 'Required' when the string is empty after trimming.
Add a range validator that returns 'Must be between 0 and 100' when the number is below 0 or above 100.
Create src/lib/validators.test.js with at least 6 cases covering empty, boundary, and valid values.
Run the unit tests and confirm all cases pass.

K-003532.example: The range validator returns 'Must be between 0 and 100' for 101 and returns null for 100. The test file has 6 cases and all of them pass.
K-003532.check: npx vitest run src/lib/validators.test.js prints 'Tests 6 passed (6)' with exit code 0.
traps: Returning false instead of null breaks the truthy check that decides whether to show a message.
Testing only mid-range values misses the 0 and 100 boundaries where bugs usually hide.
Coercing an empty string to 0 hides a missing value, so check for empty input first.

steps.do: Give each error span in EditableTable.jsx an id built from the row id and field name, such as err-7-email.
Set aria-describedby on the matching input to that same id only when an error exists.
Set role='alert' on the error span so the message is announced when it appears.
Run the accessibility check against the running table page and confirm it reports no violations.
Count the lines that set aria-invalid in the test file to confirm the attribute is covered.

K-003533.example: Row 7's email error renders with id err-7-email and the input has aria-describedby='err-7-email'. The axe run reports 0 violations for the table page.
K-003533.check: npx axe prints '0 violations' for the table page and grep -c prints a number of 1 or more.
traps: Using the row index in the id collides with other rows after a removal, so use the stable row id.
Leaving aria-describedby set when no error exists points to a missing element.
A red border alone does not tell screen readers that the cell is invalid.

steps.do: Compute the error count by taking the number of keys in the errors object in EditableTable.jsx.
Set the disabled prop on the Save button to true whenever the error count is greater than 0.
Add a test that types an invalid value and checks that the Save button is disabled.
Run only the save-related tests in the component test file.
Check that the component file is formatted correctly.

K-003534.example: After an empty name in row 2, the errors object has one key and the Save button renders with disabled set. The filtered test run prints 'Tests 1 passed'.
K-003534.check: npx vitest run -t save prints 'Tests 1 passed' and the rendered Save button has the disabled attribute.
traps: Counting rows instead of error keys disables Save for tables that are fully valid.
Setting an error to undefined leaves the key in place, so delete the key when the error clears.
A disabled button ignores clicks, so show the reason in visible text near the button.

steps.do: Keep a touched set in state and add the cell key to it when that input fires onBlur.
Show the error only when the cell key is in the touched set and the validator returns a message.
Remove that cell's error inside onChange so the message clears as soon as the value becomes valid.
Run only the blur-related tests in the component test file.
Run eslint on the component to catch unused variables left over from the change.

K-003535.example: Focusing the empty name cell and pressing Tab adds its key to touched and shows 'Name is required'. Typing a valid name removes the message on the next change event.
K-003535.check: npx vitest run -t blur prints 'Tests 1 passed' and the error text is in the DOM after blur.
traps: Validating on every change shows errors before the user finishes typing.
Forgetting to add the key to touched means blur does nothing.
Clearing errors only on submit leaves stale messages on screen after the user fixes a value.

steps.do: Install react-hook-form as a project dependency.

In the component file, call useForm<FormValues>({ defaultValues: { rows: [{ qty: 1 }] } }) to get control and formState, then call useFieldArray({ control, name: 'rows', keyName: 'key' }) and read fields from its result.
Inside the map over fields, call register('rows.' + index + '.qty', { required: 'Quantity is required', min: 1 }) on the input for that row, where index is the map index.
Inside the same map, read formState.errors.rows?.[index]?.qty and render its message in a element next to that row's input.
Run the production build to confirm the form compiles without import errors.

K-003536.example: register('rows.0.qty', { required: 'Quantity is required', min: 1 }) reports its message at formState.errors.rows[0].qty. The npm run build command exits with code 0 after the change.
K-003536.check: npm install adds react-hook-form under dependencies in package.json and npm run build exits with code 0.
traps: Rows that already have an id field clash with the default keyName of useFieldArray, so pass a different keyName.
Mixing useState and register for the same field leaves two sources of truth.
Forgetting the generic type on useForm loses type hints in editors that use TypeScript.

steps.do: Confirm the token file defines the select font size variable.
Render the Select component in a Playwright test and read its computed font-size.
Assert the computed font-size equals 1rem (16px) in the spec file.
Run the unit test that checks the token is consumed by the Select component.

K-003537.example: tokens.css defines --font-size-select: 1rem; the Playwright spec calls getComputedStyle on the select and expects '16px'. The spec passes, showing the token reached the DOM.
K-003537.check: Playwright reports '1 passed' and Vitest reports 'Tests 1 passed (1)' with no failed assertions.
traps: Checking the CSS file alone does not prove the component uses the token.
Comparing rem values as strings fails; compare the computed pixel value, such as 16px.
Forgetting to set the root font size makes 1rem differ from 16px in some test environments.

steps.do: List the foreground and background color tokens used by the select.
Run axe against the rendered select page to report color-contrast violations.
Confirm the axe output contains zero color-contrast violations for the select node.
Record the measured contrast ratio and confirm it is at least 4.5:1 for 16px text.

K-003538.example: --color-select-text is #1a1a1a on #ffffff, a ratio of 17.4:1. axe reports zero color-contrast violations on the select.
K-003538.check: axe prints 'violations: 0' for color-contrast and the measured ratio is 4.5:1 or higher.
traps: Checking only the hex values by eye misses hover and focus states that use different tokens.
A ratio computed for the placeholder text may differ from the selected-value text; test both.
Axe needs the component rendered in a browser, so a static render test does not prove contrast.

steps.do: Find the token override file for the dark theme.
Run the theme snapshot test that renders Select under the dark theme.
Assert the rendered select background uses the dark token value #0f172a.
Run the type check to confirm the theme token keys match the TypeScript token type.

K-003539.example: The dark theme sets --color-select-bg to #0f172a; the Jest test asserts the computed background equals rgb(15, 23, 42). tsc exits with no errors.
K-003539.check: Jest prints 'Tests: 1 passed, 1 total' and tsc prints no output with exit code 0.
traps: A theme file that exists but is not imported by ThemeProvider has no effect.
Hex values and rgb() values are different strings; normalize before comparing.
Missing token keys often produce undefined styles instead of errors at runtime.

steps.do: Run the token build script that writes the compiled CSS.
Count the select custom properties in the generated stylesheet.
Confirm the count is 12 and the expected names are present.
Run the build check that compares the generated file hash to the committed snapshot.

K-003540.example: The build writes dist/tokens.css; grep counts 12 lines containing --select-, matching the 12 select tokens in the source JSON. The hash matches the snapshot value.
K-003540.check: grep -c prints 12 and the sha256sum output matches the value in the snapshot file.

A count of matching lines can include comments; check the names, not just the number.
A hash mismatch after a legitimate token change is expected; update the snapshot deliberately.

steps.do: Find the select font-weight and line-height token definitions.
Run the Playwright test that reads computed font-weight and line-height in a real browser.
Confirm the list output reports 1 passed and 0 failed, which means computed font-weight is 500 and line-height is 24px.

K-003541.check: Playwright list reporter prints '1 passed' and 0 failed for tests/select-type-metrics.spec.ts.
traps: Unitless line-height such as 1.5 computes to a pixel value, so compare the computed px value, not the token string.
Font-weight tokens can be strings like 'medium' in CSS; the computed value is numeric 500.
Tests that skip the browser cannot read computed styles and give false passes.

steps.do: Find the select height and padding token definitions.
Run the Playwright test that measures the rendered select bounding box in a real browser.
Confirm the list output reports 1 passed, which means the bounding box height is at least 44px.
Run the Lighthouse accessibility audit on the select story and save the JSON report.
Read the accessibility category score from the saved report; it must be 1.

K-003542.check: Playwright list reporter prints '1 passed' for tests/select-target-size.spec.ts, and jq prints 1 for the accessibility category score.
traps: Padding plus border can push the rendered height above the token value; measure the bounding box, not the token.
Converting 2.75rem to px assumes a 16px root size; confirm the root font size in the test.
A passing unit test does not measure touch target size; a browser measurement is required.

steps.do: Install dependencies if node_modules is missing.
Run svelte-check over the whole project at error threshold.
Search the signup page for every bound input.
Read the output and confirm there are no errors.

K-003543.check: Output ends with 'svelte-check found 0 errors and 0 warnings' and the command exits with code 0.

A Svelte 5 component cannot mix export let props with $props() in one file, so pick one style.
Do not treat warnings as a pass when the threshold is set to error.

Confirm the Playwright config sets baseURL.
Run only the empty-submit spec with the line reporter.

Read the summary line and confirm it passed.

K-003544.check: Playwright prints '1 passed', grep prints 2 or more, and the URL stays at /signup after the click.

Put the base URL in playwright.config.ts instead of hardcoding localhost in every goto call.

Run the validation spec once without watch mode.
Run the full test suite to catch regressions.
Check the pass count in the summary.

K-003545.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 4 passed (4)' and 'Test Files 1 passed (1)', and npm test exits with code 0.

Write one test per rule: empty, too short, bad format, and valid.
Assert the exact message string, because toBeTruthy passes for any error text.

Run the spec that submits the empty form and then scans the page with axe.
Count the aria-invalid attributes in the signup page.
Check which inputs reference an error element through aria-describedby.
Read the axe result and confirm it reports zero violations.

K-003546.check: Playwright prints '1 passed', the grep count equals the number of bound inputs (3 in this page), and the axe violations array is empty.

Red error text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background.
A message without an id that aria-describedby points to looks fine on screen but fails for screen reader users.

steps.do: Start the dev server.
POST an empty email with an Origin header and capture only the status code.
POST the same empty request and read the HTML body for the error text.
POST a valid email and password to confirm the success path.
steps.cmd: curl -s -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} -X POST http://localhost:5173/signup -H Origin:http://localhost:5173 -d email=a@b.co -d password=[REDACTED]

steps.do: Check that the status code of the invalid request is 400.

K-003547.example: An empty email POST makes the action return fail(400, { email: 'Email is required' }), so the first curl prints 400 and the re-rendered HTML contains 'Email is required'. The valid POST returns a redirect that curl reports as 303.
K-003547.check: The first POST prints 400, the second response body contains 'Email is required', and the valid POST prints 303 or 200.

Fields belong in the request body sent with -d, because query-string values are ignored by the action.
A fail() call must return a 4xx status, or the client treats the invalid submit as success.

steps.do: Count the bound inputs in the signup page.
Count the error message elements that use the data-error convention.
Run the timing spec that requires an error within 200ms of blur.
Compare the two counts and confirm they are equal.

K-003548.example: The page has 3 bind:value lines and 3 data-error spans, so the counts match. error-timing.spec.ts blurs the email field and expects the message to be visible with timeout: 200.
K-003548.check: The first two commands print the same integer, such as 3 and 3, and Playwright prints '1 passed'.

Small models pick a timeout such as 2000ms and call it fast, but the limit must be set explicitly to 200 in the expect call.
A count mismatch means at least one field has no error element, so fix the page before trusting the spec.

steps.do: Create the file ErrorStateView.swift in the modal folder.
Write struct ErrorStateView: View with let message: String and let retry: () -> Void, showing the message in ContentUnavailableView with a Button('Try Again', action: retry) under actions.
Apply .frame(minHeight: 44) to the Try Again button so the tap target is at least 44pt tall.
Check that the minimum height of 44 appears in the file.
Check that the Try Again label appears exactly once.

K-003549.check: rg -n prints one matching line with the line number of minHeight: 44, and rg -c prints 1.

steps.do: Create the file ModalContainer.swift in the modal folder.

In ModalContainer.swift, attach .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]), .interactiveDismissDisabled(isLoading), and .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: isLoading) to the sheet content, where isLoading is a Bool derived from the state.
Measure: count the interactiveDismissDisabled modifiers and expect the number 1.
Measure: count the presentationDetents modifiers and expect the number 1.
Measure: confirm the 200ms animation duration with the number 1.

K-003550.check: Each rg -c command prints the number 1 for ModalContainer.swift.

steps.do: Print the installed React version.
Confirm React is at least 18.0.0 by checking the package.json range.
If the version is 18.0.0 or higher, plan to wrap each tab panel in React.Suspense with a fallback. If it is below 18, plan per-panel isLoading state instead.

K-003551.example: node prints 18.3.1, so the plan uses React.Suspense with a fallback prop on each TabPanel. A version of 17.0.2 would switch the plan to a boolean isLoading state in each panel.
K-003551.check: node -p prints a version starting with 18 or higher, and plan.md names React.Suspense as the chosen approach.

steps.do: Check whether any tab markup already uses role tablist or tabpanel.
Plan role tablist on the container, role tabpanel on each panel, and aria-busy true on the panel while loading.
Plan a status element with aria-live set to polite and text color at a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background.
Run an axe check against the settings page on a running dev server.

K-003552.example: The plan sets aria-busy="true" on the tabpanel and uses an aria-live polite status with text at 4.6:1 contrast. npx axe on localhost:3000/settings should report 0 violations.
K-003552.check: npx axe http://localhost:3000/settings reports 0 violations, and the plan lists aria-busy and aria-live with a 4.5:1 contrast target.

steps.do: Check whether a tab state type already exists in the codebase.
Create the directory for the tab components.
Create the types file, then write by hand the union of idle, loading, ready and error as export type TabLoadState.
Print the types file to confirm the union appears once.
Confirm the project type checks with the union in place.

K-003553.example: The file defines export type TabLoadState equal to idle, loading, ready or error. cat prints that one line, and npx tsc --noEmit then exits with no errors.
K-003553.check: npx tsc --noEmit prints nothing and exits 0, and cat src/components/Tabs/types.ts prints exactly one TabLoadState union line.

steps.do: Search for any existing delay or timer constants in the tab code.
Create plan.md, then write by hand SPINNER_DELAY_MS = 200, with the spinner shown only after that delay.
Confirm the constant is recorded with the value 200.
Add two tests by hand: one resolves at 150ms and expects no spinner, and one resolves at 250ms and expects a spinner. Then run the tab tests.

K-003554.example: The plan sets SPINNER_DELAY_MS to 200. A test renders a panel that resolves in 150ms and expects no spinner, then a second test resolves in 250ms and expects one. Jest reports 2 passed.
K-003554.check: npx jest --testPathPattern tabs reports 2 passed tests for the delay cases, with 0 failed.
traps: Choosing 0ms makes the spinner flash on fast responses. Using a delay above 500ms makes slow loads look broken.

steps.do: Search for existing uses of useTransition or startTransition in the codebase.
Find the call site of setActiveTab, which changes the tab index.
Create plan.md, then write by hand: wrap setActiveTab in startTransition so the current panel stays visible, and show the spinner only after 1000ms of pending.
Confirm the 1000ms timeout is recorded in plan.md.
Run the Playwright tab loading spec to confirm the switch keeps the old panel visible.
